issues.description: validate_conda substring match accepts any binary whose --version output contains 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba'
issues.detail: The membership test `tool in out.decode().lower()` matches anywhere in the string. A script named 'anaconda-helper' or output like 'not a conda tool' passes. Stating the invariant precisely: the executable identifies itself as one of these tools on its first whitespace-separated token. Anchor the check (e.g., parse the first token, or use startswith) so the validator actually proves what its docstring claims.

issues.description: Filter '*.exe' on the browse dialog excludes valid Unix conda executables
issues.detail: On macOS and Linux, conda/mamba/micromamba have no .exe extension, so a user clicking Browse cannot select their actual binary. The filter should be platform-conditional (or simply 'All files') with .exe preferred only on Windows. As written, the feature is unusable via the picker on the majority of supported platforms.

issues.description: Nested get_conf with inline conditional obscures the control-flow invariant
issues.detail: The new fallback uses a conditional expression inside an argument to get_conf, which makes the precondition (`custom_conda` enabled AND `conda_path` non-empty) hard to read at a glance. A literate rewrite—read the flag, read the path, then a single `if flag and path: conda_exe = path`—states the invariant the code is enforcing. Same behavior, readable without running it.

issues.description: validate_conda runs a subprocess on every keystroke without caching or timeout
issues.detail: If validate_callback is invoked on each text change, every edit spawns the executable with --version. This is not asymptotically wrong, but the constants (process spawn, no timeout) are unpleasant if the path points to a slow or hung binary. Consider validating on focus-out or adding a short timeout to communicate(). Premature to optimize aggressively, but worth a guard.

issues.description: No unit tests accompany validate_conda or the new fallback branch
issues.detail: Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it. The substring-match flaw above would have been caught by a two-line test feeding a fake binary whose --version prints 'not conda'. A small test of validate_conda (empty string, missing file, non-exec file, fake conda, real-ish conda) and one test of the kernelspec fallback would lock the invariants down.

review.summary: The change is small and the algorithmic content is modest, so the rigor questions are mostly about invariants and inputs rather than complexity. The dominant issue is that `validate_conda` claims to identify the executable as conda/mamba/micromamba but actually performs an unanchored substring match on the full --version output—the stated invariant does not hold. Secondary: the file-dialog filter '*.exe' silently disables the Browse path on Linux/macOS, and the new kernelspec fallback would read more clearly with the precondition stated as a plain `if`. No measurements were taken, but a per-keystroke subprocess with no timeout is worth a guard. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED, leaning RIGOROUS once the validator is anchored and a handful of tests are added.
